chief_complaint: sudden severe headache and intraparenchymal lobar hemorrhage in a 24-year-old
hpi_details: 24F presenting with sudden occipital hemorrhage and subarachnoid blood with bag of worms tangle of abnormal vessels and draining veins on CT angiography.
ideas: She thinks she is suffering from a massive migraine brought on by intense work stress and a spike in her blood pressure.
concerns: She is terrified that a blood vessel burst in her head and that she is suffering a life-threatening stroke.
expectations: She hopes to get an immediate head scan and an intravenous pain medication that will take away the unbearable pain.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Ruptured Arteriovenous Malformation (AVM) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Ruptured Arteriovenous Malformation (AVM) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for Arteriovenous Malformation AVM Rupture, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Ruptured Arteriovenous Malformation (AVM).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Ruptured aneurysm without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as prior seizures or headaches, which could represent earlier warning signs of an AVM.

boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.

teaching.one_liner: An abnormal tangle of blood vessels present since birth ('bag of worms') ruptures, causing sudden hemorrhage into the brain; unlike aneurysms, AVMs classically present in young people.
differentials: Hypertensive hemorrhage (less likely at this age)
red_flags: Prior seizures or headaches, which could represent earlier warning signs of an AVM

must_ask.say: How suddenly did this headache start, and how severe is it?
Have you ever had seizures or unusual headaches before this?
Does anyone in your family have blood vessel abnormalities in the brain?
Do you have any history of high blood pressure?

history.answer: I was hit out of nowhere with the most violent, explosive headache of my entire life about two hours ago.
It struck instantly like a lightning strike, reaching maximum ten-out-of-ten severity within two or three seconds.
It started roughly two hours ago and has stayed constant at maximum intensity; I've never experienced anything even remotely close to this.
It is centered deep in the back of my head on the left side, but the agony throbs across my entire skull and shoots down into my neck.
It feels like an unbearable, pounding explosion inside my head, easily a ten out of ten.
I felt violently nauseous right after the pain hit and vomited twice, bringing up clear fluid.
Yes, any bright light or loud noise feels like a spike driving through my head.
The right half of my vision has looked blurry and dark ever since this headache hit, but I don't see double.
My neck feels incredibly stiff and sore, and trying to tuck my chin down hurts so much I can't do it.
I haven't had any arm or leg weakness, numbness, slurred speech, or seizures, and I haven't blacked out.
A couple of times over the past year, I had brief throbbing headaches and shimmering lights in my vision, but nothing ever felt dangerous like this.
No, I have no tearing, red eyes, runny nose, or drooping eyelids.
Any movement, jarring, or coughing makes the pounding unbearable, and lying flat in the dark makes it only slightly more tolerable.
I swallowed two ibuprofen pills right after it started, but they didn't take off any of the edge.
I wasn't doing anything heavy; I was just sitting at home watching TV, and I haven't been drinking or lacking sleep.
No, I didn't hit my head, fall, or suffer any kind of head injury.
No, I haven't felt feverish, had chills, or noticed any skin rash.
No one around me is sick or complaining of headaches, and we don't have any gas heating appliances.
I was diagnosed with high blood pressure about a year ago, which surprised me because I'm young, but I take my blood pressure pill daily.
No, I have never had cancer, HIV, or any condition affecting my immune system.
I thought this was just the worst migraine of my life caused by stress and my blood pressure acting up.
I'm terrified that an artery burst in my brain and that I might die or end up paralyzed.
I just want an emergency brain scan and something strong in an IV to stop this blinding pain right now.
I have hypertension and mild high cholesterol, but no other chronic illnesses.
I have never had surgery, and I've never been hospitalized before today.
I take lisinopril 10 milligrams once every morning, and I don't take any other prescriptions, herbs, or vitamins.
I don't have any known allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
My mother has high blood pressure, but no one in my family has had brain aneurysms, vascular malformations, or brain bleeds.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used e-cigarettes.
I have an occasional glass of wine on weekends, but I never use recreational drugs or stimulants.
I work as a graphic designer and live with a roommate in an apartment.
My last menstrual period began two weeks ago and was normal; I use condoms reliably and there is no possibility I am pregnant.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 154/92 mmHg, pulse 76 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, temperature 36.8°C, and SpO2 99% on room air.
Young adult female lying in bed in acute distress, grimacing and shielding her eyes from the room lighting due to intense head pain.
Alert and oriented to person, place, and time; speech is fluent and coherent though she speaks softly to avoid worsening the pain.
Pupils are equal, round, and briskly reactive to light; funduscopic exam reveals crisp optic disc margins without papilledema; confrontation testing reveals a right homonymous visual field deficit.
Cranial nerves III through XII are grossly intact with symmetric facial movements, full extraocular motion without nystagmus, and intact gag reflex.
Marked resistance and pain on passive neck flexion; positive Kernig and Brudzinski signs bilaterally.
Motor strength is 5/5 across all muscle groups in both upper and lower extremities with normal tone and no pronator drift.
Sensory examination to light touch and pinprick is fully intact and symmetric throughout all dermatomes.
Biceps, triceps, patellar, and Achilles reflexes are 2+ bilaterally; plantar responses are flexor bilaterally.
Finger-to-nose and rapid alternating movements are smooth and accurate bilaterally; formal gait evaluation is deferred due to severe distress.
No tenderness on palpation or percussion over the frontal or maxillary sinuses.
